title: Pawns of Destiny
reviewNotes: Three branches from the five-piece phase after ...Rc2+ at 101 seconds. Winning Kd7 crossing and h-file approach reaches h8=Q ...Rxa7, a checked queen-versus-rook win. Corner shelter Kb8 ...Rb2+ still wins until Ka8 gives away the win; ...Rh2 holds. Independent Kd6 ...Rc8 comparison draws. This is a second source clip titled Pawns of Destiny, not a duplicate source ID.
transcript: The genius of white comes up with A7, and the pawn is only one step away from getting a new queen. But black is not naive enough to think that this is over. So he starts giving some checks to the white king. Now, of course, if the white king was to come back down, we would have a repetition. So the king has to try and going up. Now there are no more safe checks for the rook, but black has a very clever idea. King to B1. Now preparing a skewer with rook to A2. If you get a queen, you're going to lose it right away. But this one move without a check allows white [music] to push the H pawn. And now both pawns are only one step away from promoting. Black realizes that it cannot stop both promotions. But at the same time, look at how open this board is. As long as black can keep checking the white king, there's going to be no promotion. White needs to find a way to stop the checks and bring the king to help the pawns. So it plays king to B4. Now, of course, black cannot take this pawn because otherwise the other one is going to promote. But black can keep giving more checks. It is important to notice that white can never step towards the center of the board because otherwise, after, for example, this check and the king moves, the rook is going to be able to fly to the last rank and stop both promotions at the same time. But if the king goes to A5, now the rook is unable to go to the last rank because that's defended by the pawn. So the rook has to keep checking. The king keeps going up, and eventually it reaches the pawn. But actually we realize that finding shelter with the pawn doesn't help at all. After the king hides behind the pawn, now rook to H2 is going to stop the other promotion, and the king is preventing this pawn from pushing. So is this it? Is this game a draw? Well, not exactly. White plays king to D7, a seemingly mysterious move. Didn't we say that we cannot go towards the center? Well, the situation has changed. The rook cannot go to the last rank because it's defended by the king. So, the king starts marching to the other side of the board, and all of a sudden then black realizes that there is a problem. On this side of the board, there is no black king. And the black king was supporting the checks of the black rook. So, the king starts marching down, and again, it is impossible for the black rook to go to the last rank. And once the king reaches the rook, [music] there are not going to be any more safe checks. There is no black king to support a check on h2, which means that black will have to stop one of the two pawns, but the other one is going to promote, and white is going to win this game.
